title: steerwright setup: what counts, limits, name, repo

questions.title: What counts as one project
questions.question: What should count as one project on the steerwright main page?
questions.why: Discovery found 63 recently active folders (worktrees already folded in). The WIP limit and the weekly reviews work per project, so this decides whether the page reads as 63 rows or about a dozen.

options.label: Group them
options.consequence: Plugins, packages and films each roll up into a portfolio line (e.g. 'plugin family', 'package modernization'); big standalone works (Arvum, Tiny Colony, each film) stay separate. About 10-15 rows.

options.label: Every repo or folder
options.consequence: 63 rows; the WIP limit only makes sense if it is large.

options.label: Only what I add
options.consequence: Discovery proposes; nothing enters until you accept it.

guess.why: 63 rows break the WIP limit and the weekly review; your plugins move as one family of work.

one_pager.text: Found today: Arvum Electrum, Tiny Colony, the siege news film, about 40 wright plugins, about 8 packages, homework, the music projects and the chain runs (book learnings, technique harvest).

questions.title: WIP limit on active projects
questions.question: How many projects may be active at once before steerwright warns?
questions.why: Above the limit, the main page warns and weekly reviews propose tabling the quietest projects. The research suggests 3 for one person, but your agents can push several at once.

options.label: Limit of 3
options.consequence: The research default; most projects would get tabled.

options.label: Limit of 5
options.consequence: Two or three main works plus a couple of side lines.

options.label: Limit of 8
options.consequence: Loose; it would warn only when things sprawl.

guess.why: With grouping and agents doing the doing, your attention, not the hands, is the limit; 5 is between the research's 3 and your actual spread.

questions.title: Stall rule
questions.question: After how many weeks without progress should the review suggest tabling a project?
questions.why: This is the kill criterion the weekly review checks. It only suggests tabling; you still decide on the review page.

options.label: 2 weeks
options.consequence: Aggressive; good for a small WIP limit.

options.label: 4 weeks
options.consequence: The default in the research notes.

options.label: 8 weeks
options.consequence: Gentle; long creative pauses stay active.

guess.why: A month of silence usually means the project is parked already, just not on purpose.

questions.title: Where the registry lives
questions.question: Where should the project registry (projects.json, review history, post-mortems) live?
questions.why: The registry is the only state steerwright writes. The siblings keep theirs in ~/.askwright, ~/.chainwright and ~/.grindwright.

options.label: The everlast vault
options.consequence: Synced with your other records; post-mortems sit beside your notes.

guess.why: Matches the siblings; the vault can get an export later.

questions.title: Name
questions.question: Keep the name steerwright?
questions.why: It names the repo, the plugin and the skill, so changing it later costs a rename everywhere.

options.label: finishwright
options.consequence: Says the goal: finish, table or drop.

guess.why: It reads well beside chainwright and grindwright.

questions.title: Repository
questions.question: Should the repo stay private for now?
questions.why: Making it public later is easy. The registry is never in the repo; only the code and references are.

options.label: Private for now
options.consequence: Go public after it has been used for a few weeks.

options.label: Public now
options.consequence: Released like the other wright plugins.

guess.why: The kickoff said private until you say otherwise; it reads all your project names, so it should prove itself first.

questions.title: Weekly review trigger
questions.question: Should the weekly review run on a schedule, or only when you ask?
questions.why: A scheduled task would open review pages by itself each week; the kickoff says to ask before adding any scheduled task.

options.label: When I ask
options.consequence: Run sw.py review or say 'weekly review'.

options.label: Every week by itself
options.consequence: A scheduled task makes the review pages for every active project.

guess.why: Prove the reviews are useful before automating them.
